summary: Since January 2022 Tajikistan has waived visas for citizens of 52 countries for stays of up to 30 days; its Consular Department's country table gives 30 days visa-free to citizens of the EU, US, Canada, Australia and Japan, and no time limit to citizens of Russia, Belarus, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Moldova, Ukraine and Georgia. Citizens of the 129 countries and territories on the evisa.tj nationality list (as of 7 October 2026), including the UK, can apply online for an eVisa (with an optional GBAO permit); the rest apply at a Tajik embassy.

currencyLimits.text: The UK Foreign Office says cash above USD 10,000 (or the equivalent) must be declared on entry, with documents showing where the money came from, that up to USD 3,000 can be taken out without a declaration, and that you should keep your entry declaration until you leave.

notes: The UK says customs declaration forms are available in Russian and English, and recommends keeping your entry declaration until departure to prove how much money you brought in; failing to declare can mean fines or delays at the border.
The UK says the possession or use of drones is prohibited unless you have permission from the Tajik National Security Committee; without it you may be detained and your equipment confiscated.

Australia's Smartraveller says some medications, including codeine, are restricted in Tajikistan: check that yours are legal, and declare all medicines and other restricted items on arrival, or you could face charges.

payments.text: The UK calls Tajikistan a mainly cash-only economy where very few businesses accept credit cards. ATMs are increasingly common in Dushanbe and larger towns but absent in rural areas, and most accept only Visa. US dollars are the easiest foreign currency to exchange, but official exchange booths may refuse damaged or marked notes and dollars issued before 2013.

safety.text: The UK Foreign Office says pickpocketing is common in crowded places such as markets and public transport and that terrorists are likely to try to carry out attacks in Tajikistan; Canada's travel advice says the land border with Afghanistan has been closed since the Taliban takeover in 2021.

tips.text: The Gorno-Badakhshan Autonomous Region (GBAO) needs its own permit on top of your visa or visa waiver, according to UK, Canadian and Australian travel advice. eVisa applicants select it in the same application on evisa.tj; the UK Foreign Office says others can get it from a Tajik embassy before travelling or, in Tajikistan, from the Consular Department of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

The UK says you need a permit, in addition to your visa, to travel within 20 km of the Afghan border in the Khatlon region, applied for at the Consular Department of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs in Dushanbe, and that the government sometimes stops issuing GBAO permits to tourists at short notice.

The UK advises bringing enough cash for your entire stay or withdrawing it in Dushanbe before heading to other regions. It says very few businesses accept credit cards, there are no ATMs in rural areas, and official exchange booths may refuse damaged or marked notes and US dollars issued before 2013.

Tajikistan's MFA says visitors under the visa waiver must register with the authorities within 10 working days of arrival, and that eVisa holders are exempt from registration. The UK Foreign Office says hotels are no longer permitted to register guests, so register at the OVIR office in Dushanbe.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Tajikistan?
faq.answer: Tajikistan's Consular Department lists citizens of all EU countries, the US, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, Japan and South Korea as visa-free for up to 30 days, and citizens of Russia, Belarus, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Moldova, Ukraine and Georgia as entering with no time limit set. British and Israeli citizens need a visa and can apply for the eVisa at evisa.tj, as can citizens of all 129 countries and territories on the portal's nationality list (as of 7 October 2026); the rest apply at a Tajik embassy.

faq.question: Do US citizens need a visa for Tajikistan?
faq.answer: No. US passport holders can enter Tajikistan visa-free for up to 30 days. For a stay of more than 30 days, Tajikistan's MFA says you need a visa suited to the purpose of the trip before travelling.

faq.question: What is the GBAO permit and when do I need it?
faq.answer: The Gorno-Badakhshan Autonomous Region requires a separate permit in addition to a Tajik visa or visa waiver, according to UK, Canadian and Australian travel advice. eVisa applicants add it for USD 20 during the online application; the UK Foreign Office says others can get it from a Tajik embassy before travelling or from the Consular Department of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs in Tajikistan.

faq.question: How much does the Tajikistan eVisa cost and how long does it take?
faq.answer: The single-entry tourist eVisa carries a USD 30 consular fee under Tajikistan's consular fee table (USD 50 for multiple entry), is valid for 90 days and allows a stay of up to 60 days; apply at evisa.tj, where the amount charged is shown at payment. Adding the GBAO permit costs USD 20 more. The portal does not state a processing time and suggests applying two weeks before the trip.

faq.question: Can I enter Tajikistan overland with an eVisa?
faq.answer: Yes. Tajikistan's eVisa portal says e-visa holders can enter through all border points. Canada's travel advice says the land border with Afghanistan has been closed since the Taliban takeover in 2021.
